- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; adjust downward by 1–3% and add 1–2 day lag correction.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >3%), model overreacts; cap subsequent forecast values at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to correct; reduce forecast slope downward by 0.5–1.5 units per 5-day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits short-term momentum; dampen forecast tail (last 5 days) by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or declining.
